data.hypothesis: The selected four-lane parent and prior eight-lane candidate were both correct, with reported means of 0.1918 s and 0.1503 s respectively, but the observations do not include a per-thread breakdown. A two-lane interleave tests whether fewer active-state checks and lower register demand can retain useful instruction-level parallelism; it may instead expose more recurrence latency than wider groups.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use prior widths as comparison points, not proof that wider interleaving itself caused a gain; this candidate tests the narrower-width tradeoff.
memory_lessons.claim: The reported four-lane and eight-lane candidates were both correct and had means of 0.1917555 s and 0.1503027 s respectively; observations do not separate one-thread from four-core-budget results.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this two-lane candidate with the same baseline and four-lane parent at one thread, and report the four-core-budget result separately.

data.notes: This is a width-two contrast to the selected width-four parent. The pair loop retains the original float coordinate expressions, per-pixel escape test and count, and recurrence operation order; a scalar loop handles any odd-width tail. The program still overwrites the output and does not alter OpenMP scheduling or compiler settings. No execution or new measurement was performed here. The available means do not establish one-thread throughput or thread scaling; use one-thread results as the main kernel comparison and report the four-core-budget result separately.
transformations: Replace four-pixel groups with two independent scalar pixel states interleaved by iteration, maintaining a separate active flag and escape count for each lane.
Keep the original x/y float coordinate calculations and recurrence operation order; process any remaining odd-width pixel with the existing scalar routine.
